overridesNotes.postcss@<8.5.19: GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93 XSS via unescaped </style> in stringify, plus GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q (<=8.5.11) and GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 (<=8.5.17) arbitrary .map file disclosure via attacker-controlled sourceMappingURL. next 16.2.x still pins postcss 8.4.31 exactly, and @tailwindcss/postcss allows ^8.5.6, so this override is what lifts next's copy. Do NOT retarget this at next 16.3: 16.3.0-preview.9 pins postcss 8.5.10, which is still vulnerable to both sourceMappingURL advisories — so the previous 'remove when next 16.3 stable lands' trigger was wrong. Remove only when next's own pinned postcss is >=8.5.18.
overridesNotes.@modelcontextprotocol/sdk>@hono/node-ser: GHSA-frvp-7c67-39w9 path traversal in serve-static on Windows via encoded backslash (%5C), fixed in 2.0.5. @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.29.0 is the LATEST published SDK and pins @hono/node-server ^1.19.9, so the fix is a major outside its range and no parent upgrade exists at all. 1.x -> 2.x is a major (Node >=20, changed serve() signature) but is unobservable here: the consuming modules (server/express.js, server/streamableHttp.js) are never imported — apps/web loads only server/webStandardStreamableHttp.js and server/mcp.js — and the advisory is Windows-only while the runtime is a Linux container. Peer hono ^4 is satisfied by our pinned 4.12.30. Last-resort condition: package is fully isolated from production code paths, present in the tree but never loaded. Remove when @modelcontextprotocol/sdk pins @hono/node-server ^2 itself.
overridesNotes.hono: Clears 8 hono advisories (GHSA-88fw-hqm2-52qc CORS wildcard-with-credentials, GHSA-hvrm-45r6-mjfj + GHSA-w62v-xxxg-mg59 jsx/cx XSS and cross-request leakage, GHSA-wwfh-h76j-fc44 serve-static traversal, plus the Lambda/ALB adapter set). @modelcontextprotocol/sdk declares hono ^4.11.4, which ALREADY allows the patched 4.12.27+, so this is a maturity CAP, not a forced upgrade — the version is inside the parent's tested range. It exists because the newest in-range hono (4.12.32) was only 29h old at the time of writing, below our 48h supply-chain bar, and pnpm offers no reliable per-package way to cap a transitive's version (minimumReleaseAgeExclude is not honoured for transitive/optional deps). 4.12.30 is 12 days old and >=4.12.27. Note hono has two parents (the SDK directly and @hono/node-server), so this is deliberately unscoped to cover both. Remove this pin at the next dependency review — once the newest in-range hono is comfortably mature, the SDK's own ^4.11.4 range resolves it correctly with no override at all.
overridesNotes.next>sharp: GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj inherited libvips CVEs (CVE-2026-33327, CVE-2026-33328, CVE-2026-35590, CVE-2026-35591), fixed in sharp 0.35.0. Reachable, not theoretical: next/image is used in both apps including the shipped portal (apps/web/components/layout/top-nav.tsx), and next/dist/server/image-optimizer.js does a bare require('sharp'), which under pnpm resolves to next's OWN sibling copy — so adding sharp as an app dependency would install a second copy that is never loaded. next 16.2.11 pins sharp ^0.34.5, which excludes 0.35.x; the first line to pin ^0.35.3 is 16.3.0-preview.9, so no stable next resolves a patched sharp today. Sentinello never calls sharp directly, so 0.35.0's removals (failOnError, paletteBitDepth, format.jp2k -> jp2, dropped install script) only matter to Next's optimizer, and Vercel already ships next+sharp 0.35.3 together on the 16.3 line. Node 24 satisfies sharp's >=20.9.0. Remove when next 16.3 stable lands and pins ^0.35.3 natively.
overridesNotes.jsdom>undici: Maturity CAP, not a security fix — there is no advisory here. jsdom 29.1.1 declares undici ^7.25.0, which resolves to 7.29.0; that was published 5 days before this pin and is inside the repo's 7-day minimumReleaseAge quarantine. 7.28.0 is 44 days old and satisfies the same ^7.25.0 range, so this stays within the parent's tested range rather than forcing a version on it. Scoped to jsdom because jsdom is the only consumer. Context: jsdom + @testing-library were added so the one remaining untested file (apps/web/components/ui/use-anchored-panel.ts, a React hook needing a DOM) could be covered, and the install itself needed a per-command --config.minimumReleaseAge=0 — not because any package being ADDED was immature (all were 90+ days old) but because any package.json edit makes pnpm re-resolve the whole graph, which trips over the already-locked @rollup/rollup-*@4.62.3 family published 3 days earlier. That override was per-command only; .npmrc and pnpm-workspace.yaml are untouched. This pin exists because the override, being global to that one command, would otherwise have let undici in at 5 days. Remove at the next dependency review, once the newest in-range undici is comfortably mature and jsdom's own ^7.25.0 resolves it correctly with no override.
overridesNotes.brace-expansion: SECURITY: clears GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp (DoS, exponential-time expansion of consecutive non-expanding {} groups, <5.0.7) and GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (DoS, unbounded expansion length causing an OOM process crash, <5.0.8), both reported as high against the previously locked 5.0.6. Sole path is minimatch@10.2.5 -> brace-expansion, and minimatch declares ^5.0.5, so the patched 5.0.8 is already inside the parent's range — this is NOT a forced upgrade. The pin exists because it is simultaneously a maturity CAP: the newest release is 5.0.9, published 2 days before this pin and inside the 7-day quarantine, and refreshing the entry required the same per-command --config.minimumReleaseAge=0 escape hatch described in the @babel/generator note (the already-locked @rollup/rollup-* family re-validating), which would otherwise have admitted 5.0.9. 5.0.8 is 9 days old and patched. Deliberately unscoped so no vulnerable copy can appear under any future parent. This REPLACES the older 'brace-expansion@>=5.0.0 <5.0.6' pin, which had become inert — it only rewrote versions nothing would select while the lockfile sat on a vulnerable 5.0.6. Remove when 5.0.9+ is mature and minimatch's own ^5.0.5 resolves a patched version with no override.
overridesNotes.@babel/generator: Maturity CAP, not a security fix — no advisory here. Covers the whole 2026-08-01 batch: @babel/generator, @babel/parser, @babel/traverse, @babel/types, browserslist>baseline-browser-mapping and browserslist>electron-to-chromium. eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1 depends on @babel/core ^7.24.4, which pulls the @babel/* siblings and (via browserslist) the two browser-data packages — all NEW to this tree. @babel/core resolved to a mature 7.29.7, but its own ^7.29.7 sibling ranges resolved to 7.29.8, published under 24h earlier. This is the same trap the jsdom>undici note describes: adding the lint plugins required a per-command --config.minimumReleaseAge=0 to get past the already-locked, already-vetted @rollup/rollup-*@4.62.3 family (6 days old, re-validated only because any package.json edit forces a full re-resolution), and that global escape hatch would otherwise have admitted six sub-2-day-old packages. 7.29.7 is 68 days old and satisfies @babel/core's ^7.29.7, so this stays inside the parent's tested range rather than forcing a version on it — and it dedupes the tree, since @babel/parser and @babel/types were ALREADY present at 7.29.7 and had gained a second 7.29.8 copy. The two browserslist children are scoped to their only consumer and sit inside its ^1.5.393 / ^2.10.44 ranges. .npmrc and pnpm-workspace.yaml are untouched. Remove all six at the next dependency review, once these versions are comfortably mature and the parents' own ranges resolve them with no override at all.
